title: Introduce presubmit cache-proxy, slim CI bootloader, and release signaler
author: Jordan Li
release_notes: Added a lightweight presubmit cache proxy to reduce CI network IO; small bootloader images for faster startup; release signaler that attaches smoke-run results to release notes. No behavioral changes to public APIs.
description:
Motivation: presubmit jobs were spending a large portion of wall-clock time waiting on remote package registries and shared artifact stores; cold CI runner startup and network IO contribute to slow feedback and flakiness. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: (1) a presubmit cache-proxy that runs as a short-lived sidecar on ephemeral CI runners to serve cached package artifacts and proxy registry requests; (2) a slim CI bootloader image (minimal toolchain + fast init) to reduce runner boot time and image pull size; (3) a release signaler utility that posts a compact smoke-run summary to the release automation pipeline so we can gate releases on an explicit lightweight acceptance check. High-level goals: reduce presubmit latency (esp. for JS/Python installs), reduce flakiness caused by transient registry errors, and attach automated smoke-run context to release notes for observability.

Description of changes:
- tools/ci/presubmit-cache-proxy/: new Go-based cache-proxy with HTTP/HTTPS proxying, local on-disk cache, LRU eviction, and simple /health and /metrics endpoints for Prometheus scraping. Configured to cache npm tarballs, pip wheels, and container layers.
- ci/bootloader/Dockerfile.{slim,helpers}: new multi-stage slim Dockerfile that installs only the runtime pieces used in fast presubmits (git, curl, tar, node/pip shim); legacy heavy boot images moved to ci/bootloader/legacy/ and retained for nightly/integration lanes.
- tools/release/signal.py: small Python script invoked by release pipeline that collects the last presubmit smoke-run status, test coverage quick snapshot, and artifact hashes; posts a structured message to Linear/release-notes webhook and adds a release annotation in the release metadata.
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml: updated to include a presubmit-proxy step that spins up the cache-proxy container via docker-in-docker, runs fast-installs against it, and tears it down.
- ci/runner-init.sh: wrapper that prefers slim bootloader images for fast lanes and falls back to legacy for full tests.
- docs/ci/cache-proxy.md: operational runbook, metrics to watch, and cost/retention guidance.

Commits (summary):
- add presubmit cache-proxy initial implementation and tests; wire up metrics
- add slim bootloader Dockerfile + helper scripts; provide migration notes
- integrate cache-proxy into presubmit workflow and runner-init
- add release signaler script and release workflow hook
- update docs and add runbook
- fix flaky test by extending network timeouts in proxy integration tests

Changed files (high level): .github/workflows/presubmit.yml; ci/bootloader/Dockerfile.slim; ci/bootloader/helpers/*.sh; tools/ci/presubmit-cache-proxy/{main.go,proxy.go,cache.go,go.mod}; tools/release/signal.py; ci/runner-init.sh; docs/ci/cache-proxy.md; tests/integration/test_proxy.go; Makefile (added targets: ci-cache-proxy-start/stop).

Checklist:
- [x] Basic unit + integration tests for cache-proxy (mock registry)
- [x] Presubmit flow validated on a subset of repos (sdk-python, redwood-docs)
- [x] Bootloader image size reduced ~45% vs legacy image
- [x] Release signaler posts to staging release webhook and attaches metadata
- [x] Operational docs + runbook included

Known limitations & tradeoffs:
- The proxy doesn't currently support authenticated private registries (will follow up in ENG-2257). For private registries the proxy can be run behind a short-lived credential forwarder (documented in runbook).
- This PR prioritizes fast presubmits; full integration lanes still use legacy images and full caches.

Review & CI notes: initial CI run failed on integration tests due to a flaky network assertion in test_proxy.go (intermittent DNS timeouts in runner images). I pushed a fix to increase DNS timeout and added retry logic in the integration harness. CI was rerun and then passed on the second run.

Review conversation (summary):
- Priya: asked for explicit eviction policy configuration and a safe default; requested an option to cap disk usage per-runner. Response: added LRU eviction + max-disk setting with default 2GB and documented how to tune per-runner via workflow inputs.
- Marcus: asked whether the release signaler could accidentally leak internal test artifact URLs; asked for structured redact rules. Response: added a sanitizer in tools/release/signal.py to strip auth tokens and S3 presigned URLs; tests added.
- Elena: requested a clearer migration plan for repos that depend on the legacy boot image; provided ci/bootloader/legacy/ with migration notes and a Makefile target to rebuild legacy images.
- Security review (quick): validated that proxy does not persist credentials and that traffic is restricted to ephemeral runners; added e2e smoke to assert no credentials written to disk.

CI matrix behavior and results:
- presubmit unit: pass
- proxy integration: initial fail (test_proxy.go flaky DNS), rerun pass
- lint: pass
- e2e-smoke (slim): pass
- release-signal unit: pass

Observability and SLOs:
- New metrics: ci_cache_proxy.requests_total, ci_cache_proxy.hit_ratio, ci_cache_proxy.evictions_total. Dashboards added in docs runbook and a Grafana panel suggested for SRE.
- Expected presubmit median reduction: 18-28% on sampled repositories (measured with a 2-week A/B on a staging project).

Rollout plan: deploy cache-proxy to presubmit lanes for low-risk repos (sdk-python, docs, examples) for 2 weeks, monitor hit ratio and eviction behavior; then gradually opt-in other repos. Release signaler initially enabled only for staging releases; require opt-in for production releases until we confirm sanitized payloads.

Post-merge tasks (tracked in ENG-2201):
- add private registry auth passthrough (ENG-2257)
- add auto-scaling for cache-proxy sidecars for larger runners
- backport slim bootloader to release-branches if approved by release owners

Merge: squashed and merged to main (squash commit message included perf numbers and link to runbook). No service-facing breaking changes. If we see unexpected cache stomping or disk pressure, ops can flip presubmit cache off via repository workflow input.
